span.label: priming versus framing, as this paper draws it: both activate awareness of an issue and framing additionally attributes MEANINGS to it → the same pair as drawn in drouvelis2010 / drouvelis2015 (framing RE-DESCRIBES a logically equivalent decision problem) and as reported unresolved in Hoewe2020 (where Ottati holds that framing IS a form of priming)
span.note: THREE PAPERS IN THIS CORPUS SEPARATE `priming` FROM `framing`, IN THREE FIELDS, ON THREE DIFFERENT AXES - AND NONE OF THEM CITES THE OTHERS. Economics (drouvelis, both papers) makes the criterion THE DECISION PROBLEM: framing re-describes a logically equivalent one, priming does not. Media studies (Hoewe2020) makes it AWARENESS, and reports its own field unable to settle whether the two are even distinct, quoting Ottati that `media framing constitutes a specific form of priming`. Strategic communication (this paper) makes it MEANING: the two share the activation of awareness and framing adds the attribution of meanings. **Not a disagreement about a fact - three literatures independently fixing one boundary and not noticing each other.** That is the negative space this project was built to make visible, and the schema has no relation type for `these papers partition the same pair differently`. See Q-730, and Q-632 for the missing types.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming, in strategic communication - an ACT OF SELECTION on the audience's memory: certain patterns are activated and others are left out. The exclusion is written into the definition, which is what makes a positive and a negative primer symmetrical operations here
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming as against framing, THIS FIELD'S VERSION - the two are granted the same function (activating awareness of an issue) and separated by what framing does in addition: attribute meanings. Compare the economics version, where the criterion is re-description of the decision problem, and the media-studies version, where it is awareness
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: perceived authenticity - a construct whose positive definition is a list and whose working definition is its complement. The paper says so outright: it is OFTEN ALSO DEFINED BY NEGATION, with inauthenticity as falsity, externally motivated behaviour, and reciting a script rather than expressing one's own words
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming —distinct-from→ framing
span.note: differs in: WHAT FRAMING DOES IN ADDITION: both activate awareness of an issue, and framing also directs judgment by attributing meanings to it · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE THIRD INCOMPATIBLE CUT AT THIS PAIR IN THIS CORPUS. The economics papers separate them by re-description of the decision problem; the media-studies review reports the field unable to agree and cites Ottati holding framing to BE a form of priming. See the unhoused_relations row on this record.

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — Stated as a structural requirement - priming REQUIRES both - which is more than most of this corpus's priming papers make explicit.

span.label: priming —causes→ perceived authenticity
span.note: holds when: with a POSITIVE introductory text attached to the sponsored content · direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.85 — Half of a symmetric pair. The result the paper reports is sharper than either hypothesis: the SAME sponsored content produces opposite reactions depending only on the valence of the introductory text.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming —causes→ perceived authenticity
span.note: holds when: with a NEGATIVE introductory text attached to the sponsored content · direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.85 — The other half. Two edges rather than one because the direction reverses with the prime's valence, and an edge that averaged them would describe neither condition.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: participation —causes→ perceived authenticity
span.note: holds when: only under the NEGATIVE prime - the association is not found in the other conditions · strength of the relation: 0.7 — PARTIAL support, in the paper's own word. The abstract says audience engagement `had a stronger effect on the perception of authenticity than the positive/negative valence of the introductory text`; the results section says the association holds in one of the priming conditions. The weight and the `holds_when` follow the results section.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: sponsored content —causes→ perceived authenticity
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.7 — The premise the negative prime is built on, attributed to prior work rather than shown here - hence 0.7.
